newsitem.title: FRANCE: French pharmaceutical stocks rise on Roche issue.
newsitem.headline: French pharmaceutical stocks rise on Roche issue.

text.p: Shares in French pharmaceutical stocks rose on Friday amid speculation that Swiss group Roche Holding might be preparing for an acquisition after issuing $1 billion in convertible bonds, brokers said.
Shares in Synthelabo were up 2.28 percent at 672 francs at 1012 GMT in a flat market as the company is viewed as a possible target.

Synthelabo declined comment, but cosmetics group L'Oreal said this week it considered its controlling stake in Synthelabo a handsome investment and was under no pressure to decide whether to stay in the pharmaceuticals business or quit.
Shares in Elf Aquitaine's Sanofi drugs unit were up 2.51 percent at 530 francs at 1010 GMT. Elf has said it would consider selling the subsidiary.
The pharmaceutical industry is in the midst of a consolidation highlighted by the megamerger last year of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz of Switzerland to form Novartis.
Brokers said the talk in the Paris stockmarket was that Roche might be planning an acquisition in France.
Roche declined to comment on the rumours.
Synthelabo's sales last year were 10.43 billion francs.
Sanofi's 1996 sales were 23.65 billion francs. Its pharmaceuticals turnover totalled 19.84 billion.
